text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bunds firmed in late trade amid short-covering and were expected to touch 100 this week. Dealers said they were unsettled, however, by Monday's half-point drop and were growing sceptical about how long the rally would last. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.57, up 0.24 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilt futures made a late bid for higher ground, dragged up by the Bund rally spurred by short covering. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-28/32, up 8/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond futures rallied to a new contract high of 126.04 after a wave of buying of long-dated cash bonds by non-resident houses triggered a series of stops in the futures market. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.14, up 0.30 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds and futures ended a neutral session a touch lower after a day of falls, paring losses by the close on short-covering. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.42, up 0.10 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities stood near flat at midday as dealers positioned themselves for the Treasury's 10-year note sale. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-15/32, up 10/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.77 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher after healthy demand appeared for 20-year JGBs offered through an auction. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.12, up 0.08 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market issuance continued to flow. The rally in Bunds saw a number of sizeable mark offerings emerge. KFW set a 1.5 billion mark seven-year bond to be priced 14 b.p. over Bunds, Deutsche Bank issued a 1.0 bln mark zero-coupon 30-year bond, while Essen Hypo launched a 1.0 bln mark five-year floating-rate Pfandbrief. Pemex priced its $300 million three-year bond to yield 175 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes. Late in the session, Deutsche led a $1.03 bln FRN secured by financial receivables.
